resources.string: Make sure your camera is powered on and in Bluetooth pairing or discovery mode.
Need help?
Having trouble connecting?
1. Turn on Bluetooth on both your iPhone and camera.
2. If the camera is not paired yet, enable pairing mode on the camera before tapping connect.
3. On the camera, open Network/Smartphone settings and enable location information link so GPS data can be received from the phone.
4. Make sure Location Services are enabled on iPhone and this app is allowed to access location.

5. If the camera was set up with Sony's Creators' App or Imaging Edge Mobile, it may connect without working properly. Remove the camera from the iPhone's Bluetooth settings (Settings → Bluetooth → ⓘ → Forget This Device), delete old pairings on the camera (MENU → Network → Bluetooth → Manage Paired Device) and set it up again in this app.
6. Some camera models cannot use remote control and location linking at the same time — if problems persist, open the camera's details and turn off remote control.

Precise Location authorization needed
For the app to function as intended, you need to allow precise location. Open the settings via the button and enable precise location in the settings.
Location access "Always" needed

To send GPS data to your camera while the app is in the background, location access must be set to "Always". iOS only shows this permission prompt once, so it can now only be changed in the Settings app. Open the settings via the button, tap "Location" and choose "Always".
Confirm your cameras once

iOS now handles camera pairing through its own setup sheet. Confirm your saved cameras once and everything carries over, including all your settings. Nothing is lost and you do not have to pair the cameras again.
Confirm cameras
Close and reopen Alpha GPS to confirm the remaining cameras. iOS only allows this right after the app starts.
No cameras yet
Put your camera into pairing mode, then add it. iOS shows its own list of nearby Sony cameras.
Add camera
Open Alpha GPS once
A recent update changed how iOS pairs cameras. Open the app once to confirm your cameras, otherwise it cannot connect to them. If everything already works, you can ignore this.
Your cameras are not set up yet
Alpha GPS still needs you to confirm your cameras in the iOS setup sheet. Until you do, it cannot connect to them and photos will not be geotagged.
Confirm your cameras

iOS now handles camera pairing itself, so Alpha GPS has to ask you once to confirm the cameras you already use.

Tapping Continue opens an iOS window listing them. Confirm it and everything carries over, including all your settings. Nothing is lost and you do not have to pair the cameras again.

Until you do this, the app cannot connect to your cameras.
